# `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's non-initialised `.worklog` (and can build `.worklog/.worklog`)

> **Provenance:** `discovered-from:SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (which was transferred
> from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT`, itself `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`).
> Filed separately by producer decision so the parent fix stays narrow.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/code_freeze.py` carries its **own** copy of
`_detect_worklog_dir()`. It builds ancestor candidates as `parent / ".worklog"`
for every parent and accepts any `.worklog` directory without checking that it
is initialised. Consequences:

- from a linked worktree root whose committed `.worklog/` holds only
  `config.yaml`, `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
  `<worktree>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` — a marker file that can never exist,
  so the fail-closed freeze gate silently sees "no freeze";
- from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no committed `.worklog`), a
  stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory would be selected, giving
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

The correct marker in both cases is `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

## Users

- **AI agent running `/skill:implement` from a worktree** — the implement
  workflow consults the code-freeze marker; reading the wrong path makes the
  freeze gate miss an active freeze.
  Story: *As an implementing agent in a worktree, an active code freeze must be
  detected, so I stop instead of landing a commit that the freeze forbids.*
- **Producer/operator** — an activated freeze must be effective immediately for
  every checkout.
  Story: *As the producer, when I activate a freeze, agents working in
  worktrees must observe it without extra `--worklog-dir` instructions.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs one resolution rule, not two divergent copies.
  Story: *As a maintainer, code-freeze marker resolution must not silently drift
  from `status_lifecycle`'s worklog-dir rule.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves the main marker.** With cwd at a linked
      worktree root that has a committed, **uninitialised** `.worklog/`
      (`config.yaml` only), `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.
- [ ] **AC2 — no `.worklog/.worklog` nesting.** With cwd inside
      `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, the marker path is
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` even when a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC3 — explicit `project_root` unchanged.** `code_freeze_marker_path(<root>)`
      still returns `<root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` and is unaffected by the
      cwd-based rule.
- [ ] **AC4 — one rule, not two.** `code_freeze._detect_worklog_dir()` either
      re-uses the shared resolution helper from `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
      (preferred — no duplicated walk) or mirrors it exactly, with a comment
      naming the shared rule as authoritative.
- [ ] **AC5 — unit tests.** Hermetic `tmp_path` tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` for AC1–AC3 (no real
      `git worktree`, no network), alongside the existing marker tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The `code_freeze.py` docstrings state the
      initialised-only / no-nesting rule; if resolution is shared, note it in
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` next to the `StatusLifecycle` note.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not widen the freeze semantics: this is a path-resolution fix, not a
  change to how a freeze is activated, cleared, or enforced.
- Keep the existing public API (`code_freeze_marker_path`, marker read/write
  helpers) and their `project_root` behaviour unchanged.
- Prefer re-using the shared helper over a second walk; if that would create a
  circular import, mirror the rule and reference the canonical one in a
  comment.
- Gate order: build → test → commit; no ad-hoc `pytest` — run tests through the
  test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake of the parent item)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 48) order:
  explicit `project_root` → `<cwd>/.worklog` → `<git toplevel>/.worklog` →
  `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`, each gated on `is_dir()` only.
- `code_freeze_marker_path()` (~line 90) uses that helper and falls back to
  `<cwd>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` when nothing resolves.
- The same candidate-construction defect is proven in
  `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` (parent item
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB`, AC1–AC3) — this item is the same rule applied to the
  code-freeze copy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` / marker path
  resolution (~lines 48–101).
- `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` — new worktree-layout cases
  (AC1–AC3).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — one sentence alongside the
  `StatusLifecycle` resolution note (if the rule is shared).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the shared helper is exported
  for reuse (no behaviour change expected here).

## Related work

- `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` — parent fix for `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()`
  / `worklog_dir_flag()` (same rule, `wl`-facing seam). This item should land
  after it so the shared rule exists.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`, `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine) —
  discovery chain for the original defect.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: freeze bypass stays latent** until this item is implemented, if the
  parent fix lands alone. Mitigation: the parent item's docs state the
  code-freeze copy is still defective and link here.
- **Risk: duplicated rule drifts again.** Mitigation: AC4 prefers the shared
  helper.
- **Scope-creep risk:** touching freeze activation/enforcement or adding new
  marker features — out of scope; record such ideas as separate items.
- **Assumption:** the implement workflow's freeze check is the only consumer of
  `code_freeze_marker_path()`; verified by grep during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Fold this into the parent `worklog_dir_flag` fix?**
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — filed here; the parent item stays
  narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`, relayed via
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (Appendix Q2).

data.description:
## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` builds once (Step 2), then pushes to `dev`. When the push
loses a race and is rejected non-fast-forward, `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
fetches `origin/dev`, rebases the feature branch, recomputes the commit hash
and retries the push — **without rebuilding the worktree**. The pre-push hook
then runs the full suite against the rebased tree, where `packages/shared/dist`
(gitignored, produced by the build) is stale with respect to the `dev` commits
the rebase just pulled in. The gate goes red for a condition that does not
exist in a built tree, and the item's work is stranded until a human rebuilds.

## Users

- **Dispatch agent (leaf `finish` / driven child)** — "When my push loses a
  race to a sibling push, I want the retry to gate a tree I actually built, so
  my item lands instead of failing on a `TypeError` that names a function my
  own change set never touched."
- **Producer / operator on duty** — "I want a red dev-push gate to always mean
  something real about the pushed change set, so I never spend an hour and a
  half hand-rebuilding a worktree to clear a false red."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After a successful recovery rebase inside the push loop, `finish` builds the
   rebased worktree **before** the retry push reaches the full-suite gate. A
   test simulates a non-fast-forward rejection whose rebase introduces a new
   `packages/shared` export and asserts (a) the build ran between the rebase and
   the retry push, and (b) the recorded push verdict is green/pushed.
2. A stale-dist failure is never attributed to the item's own change set. A
   test asserts that a gate failure whose symptom is a stale shared build
   (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function` — a runtime error that the
   existing load-flake retry does not match) cannot be reported as a failure of
   the pushed change set: either the run rebuilds first, or it fails closed with
   a build/resolution diagnosis naming the stale `packages/shared/dist`.
3. A genuine red introduced by the rebased commit is still reported red. A test
   pins that the rebuild does not weaken the gate: when the rebased tree really
   fails the suite, the push is blocked and the item stays `open`.
4. `finish` on a worktree whose push is rejected once still lands the commit and
   writes the terminal `completed` / `in_review` transition (no manual
   intervention).
5. A rebuild that itself fails after the rebase fails **closed**: no push, an
   actionable comment naming the build failure and the worktree, and the item is
   reset to `open` (mirroring the existing Step 2 build-failure path) — an
   unbuilt tree is never gated.
6. No extra build is paid when no rebase happened: the normal (uncontended) push
   path keeps exactly one build per `finish`, and the changed-scope gate
   (Step 3) is never re-entered by the retry loop.
7. Tests for every behaviour above are added to the `skill/implement` suite and
   pass, and the new tests fail against the pre-change implementation (no
   vacuous green).
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A dispatch whose push races another push lands its work instead of spending an
hour and a half chasing a build-staleness false-red.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing single build entry point `run_build(cwd)` so the rebuild
  inherits the current behaviour (disk-backed `TMPDIR` injection, 300 s timeout,
  no-build-script no-op for Python-only repos) — no parallel build code path.
- The rebuild runs **inside** the push retry loop, after the rebase and before
  the retry `git_push_to_dev` call; the Step 3 changed-scope gate and the
  "at most one full-suite gate per finish" property (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) must
  survive.
- Never weaken the gate: a reproducible red on the rebuilt tree still blocks the
  push.
- Stay within the module's existing retry budget semantics
  (`DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT = 5`): a rebuild failure is a hard stop, not a
  retryable transport condition.
- Worktree-only changes; no behaviour change for the main checkout.

## Existing state

- `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:12262`)
  does: fetch `origin/dev` → `git rebase origin/dev` → capture the rewritten
  hash → `_assert_push_subject` → retry `git_push_to_dev`. There is no build
  step anywhere on this path.
- `run_build` (`implement.py:9324`) is the single build entry point; `phase_finish`
  Step 2 calls it once before tests (`implement.py:12763`).
- The pre-push gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) runs the full suite for `dev` pushes,
  bound to the pushed commit via `run_tests.py --gate-commit`, resolved by
  `resolve_gate_subject` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:3697`) — normally the
  worktree in place ("cheap in-place run"), so the suite executes against the
  worktree's filesystem including its `packages/shared/dist`.
- The verdict is tree-keyed (SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG) with change-set reuse
  (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC): a pure rebase is usually served from the pre-race
  verdict, so no suite runs. When the change set fingerprint **also** differs —
  e.g. the concurrently landed commit edited the same hub file the item edited
  (`packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` in the observed case) — the key misses,
  the suite really runs, and it runs on stale `dist`.
- Existing mitigation `_is_gate_load_flake` (`implement.py:6032`) retries once on
  suite *load* errors (`Cannot find package`, `Cannot find module`,
  `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`). A stale-dist runtime `TypeError` **loads fine** and falls
  outside those patterns, and retrying the identical unbuilt tree could not help
  anyway.
- `packages/shared/dist` is gitignored and produced by `npm run build`, so it is
  invisible to the tree fingerprint: two trees with identical git content can
  carry different `dist` contents. That is precisely the mismatch this item is
  about.
- Evidence (2026-11-18, ContextHub epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9, child
  WL-0MWKY141H002LULI): two consecutive false reds in one session — attempt 1
  rebased in `508a1821e` (`isNotStarted`) → 17 × `TypeError: isNotStarted is not
  a function`; attempt 2 rebased in `ac2a2c48e` (`normalizeStartOn`) → multiple
  `TypeError: normalizeStartOn is not a function`. Both cleared with no source
  change: `git fetch origin dev && git rebase origin/dev && npm run build` →
  `finish` green. Direct proof of staleness: `grep -c normalizeStartOn
  packages/shared/dist/predicates.js` → `0` before the manual build, `2` after.

## Desired change

The item offers three mechanisms; research picks one as primary and one as a
cheap hardening, and records why the third cannot fix the defect alone.

**A — Rebuild after a recovery rebase (recommended, primary).** After the
successful `git rebase origin/dev` in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`, and
before the retry push, call `run_build(worktree_path)`. On failure, fail closed
(no retry push, failure comment naming the build stderr tail and the worktree,
item reset to `open`). Rationale: it makes the gate's subject and the build
consistent by construction, costs one build per rebase round (the rebase round
already costs a push attempt, and at most 5 rounds run), and needs no new
persistent state.

**B — Refuse to gate a tree newer than the last build (recommended hardening).**
Record the built tree SHA when the build succeeds (a `_set_finish_progress`
field / report field is enough — no new file format), and before a retry push
verify that `HEAD^{tree}` still matches it; when it does not, rebuild. This
generalises A to the other tree-changing paths that can precede a push (amend,
`git pull`, a rebase performed outside the recovery helper) at near-zero cost.
The fail-closed branch of the item's option 2 is therefore available as the
backstop without inventing a new abort source on the normal path.

**C — Rebuild-scoped cache key (rejected as a standalone fix).** The gate's key
is derived from the git tree (or the change-set patch), and `packages/shared/dist`
is gitignored, so a build-scoped key component could only be added by hashing a
build artifact into the key. That would invalidate verdicts for every unrelated
`finish` (every build produces a different `dist`), and it does not address the
actual defect: the suite *did* legitimately re-run, then failed on a stale
artifact. Keying cannot make an unbuilt tree built.

**Non-negotiable invariant (from the item):** whatever mechanism is implemented,
the push loop must never report a *source-level* test failure for a tree it did
not build.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
  (~12262) gains the post-rebase rebuild (A) / built-tree check (B); the push
  loop in `phase_finish` (~13560–13660) surfaces the rebuild in
  `report["steps"]["push"]`; `run_build` (~9324) reused unchanged;
  `_set_finish_progress` (~759) carries the built-tree marker for B.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — the existing
  non-fast-forward / load-flake harness (`_stubbed_finish`, `sandbox`) is the
  place for the AC1–AC5 tests.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — drop-in coverage for the
  recovery helper if the rebuild is asserted at helper level rather than through
  `phase_finish`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — the "A lost push race does not re-run
  the full suite" section (~2578) and the push-robustness list (~1715) need the
  post-rebase build documented alongside the change-set reuse they describe.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the false red is caused by a stale build artifact, not by a
  wrong `dev` merge. The evidence (`isNotStarted` / `normalizeStartOn` in source
  but absent from `dist`, cleared by `npm run build` alone) supports this; if a
  similar red survives a rebuild, it is a genuine regression and must stay red
  (AC3).
- **Risk — rebuild churn vs. the push-subject guard.** On game repos `npm run
  build` runs `engine:sync` first, which can advance the engine submodule and
  stage the pin/gitlink. `_assert_push_subject` refuses a push from a worktree
  with tracked uncommitted changes, so a churn-producing rebuild could turn a
  recoverable race into a `PushSubjectMismatchError`. Mitigation: snapshot the
  churn baseline before the post-rebase build (reusing `_build_churn_baseline`),
  attribute the churn as finish's own like Step 2 does, and fail closed with an
  actionable comment when the churn cannot be carried.
- **Risk — cost.** One extra build per rebase round (≤ `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT`
  = 5 rounds). Accepted: it is far cheaper than the observed false-red recovery,
  and it is not paid on the uncontended path (AC6).
- **Risk — masking.** A rebuild that *hides* a real failure would be worse than
  the bug. Mitigated by AC3's pin test and by keeping the gate's verdict
  untouched: the rebuild changes what the suite measures, never the pass/fail
  threshold.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Making the full-suite cache key build-aware
  (mechanism C), hardening the load-flake pattern list, or re-running the suite
  after every rebase are **out of scope**; each is either rejected above or worth
  its own item. Any such finding during implementation is recorded as a linked
  work item (`discovered-from:SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q`), not absorbed here.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVPI41SR008JYXL** (completed) — "Hard-fail finish on stale shared
  resolution": covers the *resolution* check (worktree `@worklog/shared` →
  main checkout's `dist`) but not the rebase-then-gate-without-rebuild ordering.
- **SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC** (completed) — "Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on
  dev pushes": its change-set reuse usually hides this defect; this item covers
  the miss case (upstream touched the same file, so the patch's pre-images
  differ) and the invariant that survives reuse.
- **SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG** (completed) — "Gate keys on the pushed tree": the
  provenance contract the rebuild must make honest.
- **SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5** (completed) — push robustness; its AC7 load-flake retry
  is the nearest existing mitigation and is deliberately narrow (load errors
  only), which is why this defect slips through it.
- **SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO** (completed) — worktree link-farm / stale dist parent of
  the stale-resolution work.
- Discovered from ContextHub **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (child WL-0MWKY141H002LULI);
  the two commits whose push triggered the rebases: ContextHub **WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV**,
  **WL-0MWMGEPY2004EDZ8**.

### Related work (automated `find-related` report)

- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** (completed) – finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward
  after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly
  — same recovery path, sibling concern (refs, not build artefacts).
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** (completed) – Push to dev from the worktree that holds
  the commit — the push subject this item's rebuild must keep honest.
- **SA-0MWHUVISS003APKM** (open) – Tests: fresh-worktree shared build
  precondition (red-first): makes `start` ensure a worktree's
  `packages/shared/dist` is built. Complementary, not overlapping: it fixes
  freshness at *start*, this item fixes freshness after a *mid-push rebase*.
  Interfaces with it through the shared build helper and its
  `shared_build` report block.
- Repository file matches: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: Which of the item's three mechanisms should the brief specify?**
  (Options: A rebuild-after-rebase; B record-the-built-tree / fail closed;
  C rebuild-scoped cache key.)
  **Recommended:** A as primary + B as hardening — A makes the gate's subject and
  the build consistent by construction for a bounded extra build per rebase
  round, B covers the other tree-changing paths cheaply; C alone cannot fix an
  unbuilt tree and would invalidate every unrelated verdict.
  **Answer (agent research, advisory until producer confirms):** A + B described
  in *Desired change*; C rejected with rationale. The acceptance criteria are
  written behaviourally (the item's invariant) so the producer can substitute B
  alone or A alone without rewriting them. Source: repo research —
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`,
  `run_build`, `_is_gate_load_flake`), `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
  (`resolve_gate_subject`), `skill/test_cache.py`
  (`compute_change_set_state`), `.githooks/pre-push`, and
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` § "A lost push race does not re-run the
  full suite".
- **Q2: Is a post-rebase rebuild failure a hard stop or a consumed retry round?**
  **Recommended:** hard stop — a failed build is a content/config condition, not
  a transient transport one, so retrying the same tree cannot help (the same
  reasoning as the existing "load flake is retried, a reproducible failure
  blocks" split).
  **Answer (agent research, advisory until producer confirms):** hard stop, per
  AC5. Source: `_is_retryable_push_transport` (`implement.py:6048`) and the
  Step 2 build-failure path (`implement.py:12786`).
- **Q3: Should the full suite re-run on the rebuilt tree even when the change-set
  verdict would be served from cache?**
  **Recommended:** no — keep the change-set reuse (it is a correctness argument
  about the patch, not about `dist`), because the rebuilt tree makes a real suite
  run (when one happens) trustworthy; re-running on every rebase would undo
  SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC's 5–18 min saving.
  **Answer (agent research, advisory until producer confirms):** keep reuse; the
  rebuild only guarantees that a *miss* is measured on a built tree. Source:
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` ~2578–2600.

## Goal

Red-first tests: pin the whole "never gate a tree you did not build" contract in
the existing `skill/implement` push-robustness harness **before** any production
change, so every later feature in this tree has a failing test to turn green.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC1a, AC1b, AC5, AC6, AC7).

## Scope

Tests only — no production change in this item. Extend the `sandbox` /
`_stubbed_finish` harness in `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py`
(a scripted non-fast-forward recovery whose rebase introduces a new
`packages/shared` export while leaving `packages/shared/dist` stale) and, where
the assertion is cleaner at helper level, `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test simulates a non-fast-forward rejection whose recovery rebase introduces a new `packages/shared` export and asserts (a) the build ran between the rebase and the retry push, and (b) the recorded push verdict is green/pushed.
- A test asserts the uncontended (no rejection) push path pays exactly one build per `finish`, and that the Step 3 changed-scope gate is never re-entered by the retry loop.
- A test asserts a failed post-rebase build produces no retry push, an actionable comment naming the build failure and the worktree, and the work item reset to `open`.
- A test asserts a stale-dist suite failure (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function` on a tree whose `packages/shared/dist` predates the rebase) is never reported as a failure of the pushed change set: the run either rebuilds first or fails closed with a build/resolution diagnosis naming the stale `packages/shared/dist`.
- Tests for every behaviour above are added to the `skill/implement` suite and pass, and the new tests fail against the pre-change implementation (no vacuous green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse the existing `sandbox` fixture and the `_stubbed_finish` monkeypatch seams; add one shared helper that scripts "rebase advances `dev` with a new shared export and leaves `dist` stale".
- Stub `run_build` / `git_push_to_dev` / `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` with call-order recording so "build between rebase and retry push" is asserted from the observed order, not from a mock's return value.
- Record the failing-red run evidence in a comment on this item (test names + the assertion each fails on).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — main harness (`sandbox`, `_stubbed_finish`, test classes).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — helper-level assertions if the rebuild is asserted inside `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — read-only reference (`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`, `run_build`, `_build_churn_baseline`).

## Deliverables

New/extended tests, all red against the current implementation, plus a comment
recording the red run.

## Dependencies

Blocks every implementation feature in this tree (test-first ordering).

data.description:
## Goal

Rebuild the rebased worktree inside the push retry loop, so the retry push can
never reach the full-suite gate with a `packages/shared/dist` older than the
`dev` commits the rebase just pulled in.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC1, AC6, the rebuild half of AC2).

## Scope

`_recover_non_fast_forward_push` only, reusing the existing single build entry
point `run_build(cwd)` — no parallel build code path. No change to the gate's
pass/fail threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a successful recovery rebase inside the push loop, `finish` builds the rebased worktree before the retry push reaches the full-suite gate: `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` calls `run_build(worktree_path)` after the rebase and before `_assert_push_subject` / `git_push_to_dev`, and the run records the post-rebase build in `report["steps"]["push"]` so a simulated non-fast-forward rejection whose rebase introduces a new `packages/shared` export is reported green/pushed.
- Churn produced by the post-rebase build is attributed as finish's own: the churn baseline is snapshotted before the build (reusing `_build_churn_baseline`) so `_assert_push_subject` cannot refuse the retry push for churn finish itself caused.
- No extra build is paid when no rebase happened: the uncontended push path keeps exactly one build per `finish`, and the changed-scope gate (Step 3) is never re-entered by the retry loop.
- A build failure after the rebase does not reach the retry push (it delegates to the fail-closed path owned by the child "Fail closed when the post-rebase build fails").

## Minimal Implementation

- Call `run_build(worktree_path)` immediately after the rebase succeeds and the rewritten hash is captured, before `_assert_push_subject`.
- Surface the outcome as a `rebase_build` block on `report["steps"]["push"]` (attempt round, worktree, exit status, duration).
- Snapshot `_build_churn_baseline(worktree_path)` before the build and fold any new churn into the run's own-churn accounting, mirroring Step 2.
- Raise/re-raise the Step 2 build-failure exception shape on failure and let the caller handle the fail-closed transition.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` (~12262), `run_build` (~9324), `_build_churn_baseline` (~4093), `_assert_push_subject`, push loop in `phase_finish` (~13560–13680).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — the red-first tests this item turns green.

## Deliverables

The post-rebase rebuild, its report surface, churn attribution, and green tests.

## Dependencies

data.title: Rebuild the rebased worktree before the retry push

data.description:
## Goal

A post-rebase rebuild that itself fails must fail **closed**: no push, an
actionable comment, and the work item reset to `open` — never a gated unbuilt
tree.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC5).

## Scope

The failure branch of the post-rebase rebuild. Mirror the existing Step 2
build-failure path; do not consume a rebase/transport retry round.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A rebuild that fails after the rebase fails closed: no retry push is attempted for that round, and an actionable comment names the build failure (`stderr` tail) and the worktree path.
- The failure is a hard stop, not a retryable transport condition: `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT` is untouched and no further rebase round runs against the same unbuildable tree.
- The work item is reset to `open` (mirroring the existing Step 2 build-failure path), never left `in-progress` with a stranded worktree.
- `report["steps"]["push"]` records the build failure (outcome, worktree, build stderr tail) so the failure is auditable after the fact.

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse the Step 2 build-failure classification and message shape; add the rebase round number and the retained worktree path.
- Call `wl_add_comment` with the stderr tail (bounded), then raise the same hard-stop exception class Step 2 raises so the leaf loop resets the item to `open`.
- Make sure the existing post-failure `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push` path still runs (local `dev` was deferred, never advanced).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` (~12262), Step 2 build-failure path (~12786), `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push`, push loop (~13560–13680).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — the fail-closed assertions this item turns green.

## Deliverables

The fail-closed branch, its comment, the `open` reset, and green tests.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Red-first tests: post-rebase rebuild contract", "Rebuild the rebased worktree before the retry push".
data.title: Fail closed when the post-rebase build fails

data.description:
## Goal

Backstop the rebuild: a finish run knows which tree it built, and a gate
failure whose symptom is a stale shared build is diagnosed as a
build/resolution problem naming `packages/shared/dist` — never attributed to
the pushed change set.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC2, the hardening mechanism B).

## Scope

The built-tree marker + the stale-dist diagnosis. No change to the verdict
cache key (mechanism C is explicitly out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The finish run records the tree SHA (`HEAD^{tree}`) of the last successful build in the finish progress/report, and a HEAD tree that no longer matches it triggers a rebuild before any dev push — including the retry push — so no push ever gates an unbuilt tree; when that rebuild itself fails the run fails closed with a stale-build diagnosis naming `packages/shared/dist`.
- A gate failure whose symptom is a stale shared build (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function`, which the existing load-flake retry does not match because the module loads fine) is reported as a build/resolution diagnosis naming `packages/shared/dist`, never as a failure of the pushed change set.
- The guard adds no build on a tree that has not changed since the last build, and the changed-scope gate (Step 3) is never re-entered.
- Tests cover the stale-tree trigger, the unchanged-tree no-op, and the diagnosis wording.

## Minimal Implementation

- Record the built tree SHA via `_set_finish_progress` (an existing field surface — no new file format) when `run_build` succeeds in Step 2 and after the post-rebase rebuild.
- Before a dev push, compare `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` with the recorded value in the worktree; on mismatch rebuild (reusing `run_build`) and update the marker, or fail closed with the diagnosis when the rebuild fails.
- Classify a gate failure whose stderr tail matches the stale-shared symptom (`TypeError: <identifier> is not a function` where the identifier resolves from `packages/shared`) into the existing build/resolution diagnosis taxonomy instead of a change-set failure.
- Keep `_is_gate_load_flake` unchanged — this is a distinct symptom, not a load error.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_set_finish_progress` (~759), `run_build` (~9324), `_is_gate_load_flake` (~6032), the push loop and gate-failure classification (~13560–13890).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_provenance.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — provenance + push-robustness tests.

## Deliverables

The built-tree marker, the freshness check, the stale-dist diagnosis, and tests.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Rebuild the rebased worktree before the retry push" (shares the post-rebase rebuild surface).
data.title: Built-tree freshness guard and stale-dist diagnosis

data.description:
## Goal

Prove the user-visible outcome end to end: a `finish` whose push is rejected
once still lands its commit and writes the terminal transition with no manual
intervention, and a genuinely red rebased tree is still reported red.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC3, AC4, AC9).

## Scope

Verification only — end-to-end tests/checks over the behaviour delivered by the
other children in this tree; no new production mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `finish` on a worktree whose push is rejected once still lands the commit and writes the terminal `completed` / `in_review` transition, with no manual intervention (single end-to-end run against a sandbox worktree and a scripted remote).
- A genuine red introduced by the rebased commit is still reported red: when the rebased tree really fails the suite, the push is blocked and the item stays `open` (the rebuild does not weaken the gate).
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (run via the test skill / the dev-push gate), with no new failures.

## Minimal Implementation

- Drive the `sandbox` harness through a complete `finish` (rejection → rebase → rebuild → retry → terminal transition) and assert the transition status/stage and the landed commit.
- Add the genuine-red pin by making the rebased tree fail on a real assertion inside the suite stub; assert `PushGateFailureError`/gate reason and `open`.
- Run the full suite through `/skill:test` and attach the result to this item's comment (never an ad-hoc `pytest`).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — end-to-end push harness.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_provenance.py` — gate verdict/provenance assertions.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — the suite entry point used by the gate (read-only reference).

## Deliverables

The end-to-end landing test, the genuine-red pin, and the green full-suite evidence.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Rebuild the rebased worktree before the retry push", "Fail closed when the post-rebase build fails", "Built-tree freshness guard and stale-dist diagnosis".
